model_annotation: The purpose of the plot is to illustrate the accuracy percentages (ACC) based on co-occurrence numbers for six different models, each represented by a unique line and marker shape. The x-axis, labeled "Co-occurrence Number," has a logarithmic scale ranging from 10^0 (1) to 10^3 (1000). The y-axis, labeled "ACC (%)," ranges from 40% to 65% and has linear tick labels with a consistent interval. The "Base" model starts with an ACC of approximately 40% at a co-occurrence number of 10^0, showing a steady increase to about 45% at 10^3. The "MEND" model begins at around 40%, rises to just above 50% by 10^1, and continues to increase to near 55% at 10^3. The "FT" model starts at about 45%, dips down near 40% at 10^1, and recovers to approximately 45% at 10^3. The "MEMAIL" model begins with an ACC just under 50%, drops slightly at 10^1, then climbs back to just over 50% by 10^3. The "IKE" model commences at around 45%, increases to about 50% near 10^1, and maintains a steady line to close to 55% at 10^3. Finally, the "ROME" model starts at approximately 65%, decreases slightly at 10^1, and then levels off at around 60% for all subsequent co-occurrence numbers. All data points are well-defined and lack peaks or sharp declines, showing a general trend of increasing accuracy as the co-occurrence number grows.
